questions.question: Who among the following was one of the court poets of the King Samudragupta?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Harisena**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Harisena** was one of the prominent court poets of the King Samudragupta.
 
• He composed the **Allahabad Pillar inscription** which is a significant source of historical information about Samudragupta's reign.
 
• Harisena praised Samudragupta as a great warrior and ruler, highlighting his military conquests and administrative skills.
 
• The **Allahabad Pillar inscription** is also known as the **Prayag Prashasti** and it provides detailed accounts of Samudragupta's achievements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **King Samudragupta:**

 
 
• Samudragupta was a ruler of the Gupta Empire, which is considered one of the golden periods in Indian history.
 
• He reigned from around 335-380 CE and is known for his military conquests, cultural achievements, and patronage of arts and literature.
 
• Samudragupta is often referred to as the "Napoleon of India" due to his extensive military campaigns and conquests.
 
• He was also known for his administrative skills and efforts in promoting trade, commerce, and cultural activities.
 
 
 
• **Allahabad Pillar Inscription (Prayag Prashasti):**
 
 
• The Allahabad Pillar inscription is an important historical document that provides a detailed account of Samudragupta's reign and achievements.
 
• It was composed by Harisena, who was a court poet and minister of Samudragupta.
 
• The inscription praises Samudragupta's military prowess, highlighting his conquests and victories over various kingdoms and tribes.
 
• It also mentions his qualities as a ruler, including his administrative abilities, patronage of arts, and benevolence towards his subjects.
 
 
 
• **Other notable court poets:**
 
 
• **Surdas:** A 15th-16th century poet and saint known for his devotional songs and poetry dedicated to Lord Krishna.
 
• **Pragyajan:** There is limited historical information available about Pragyajan, and he is not associated with Samudragupta's court.
 
• **Hariharan:** There is no significant historical evidence linking Hariharan to Samudragupta's court. Hariharan is a common name, and there could be multiple historical figures with this name.

questions.question: Where are the Ellora caves located?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aurangabad**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Ellora Caves are located in the Aurangabad district in the Indian state of Maharashtra.
 
• They are one of the largest rock-cut monastery-temple cave complexes in the world, featuring Hindu, Buddhist, and Jain monuments and artwork.
 
• The caves were designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983.
 
• Ellora represents the epitome of Indian rock-cut architecture and is famous for its monumental caves, particularly Cave 16, also known as the Kailasa temple.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ellora Caves:**

 
 
• The Ellora Caves are a series of 34 caves located near the city of Aurangabad in Maharashtra, India.
 
• These caves were excavated from the volcanic basaltic formation of Maharashtra's Western Ghats and feature an extraordinary array of sculptures and architectural styles.
 
• Ellora is renowned for the coexistence of three major Indian religions: Hinduism, Buddhism, and Jainism, represented through its unique cave temples and monasteries.
 
• The most famous of the Ellora caves is the Kailasa temple (Cave 16), which is a single monolithic rock excavation and one of the largest of its kind in the world.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO World Heritage Sites:**
 
 
• UNESCO World Heritage Sites are landmarks or areas with legal protection by international treaties and are designated by the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO).
 
• These sites are recognized for their cultural, historical, scientific, or other forms of significance and are considered important to the collective interests of humanity.
 
• India is home to 40 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including the Taj Mahal, Qutub Minar, and the Ajanta Caves.
 
 
 
• **Rock-cut Architecture:**
 
 
• Rock-cut architecture involves the creation of structures, buildings, and sculptures by excavating solid rock where it naturally occurs.
 
• Examples of rock-cut architecture include the Ajanta and Ellora Caves, Petra in Jordan, and the rock-hewn churches of Lalibela in Ethiopia.
 
• This type of architecture is significant as it showcases the advanced engineering and artistic skills of ancient civilizations.

questions.question: The literacy rate is defined by the percentage of the population of a given age group that can ___.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Read and Write**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **literacy rate** is a measure of the percentage of people in a specific age group who can **read and write** with understanding, in any language. 
 
• It reflects the basic educational level of a population, indicating their ability to engage with written content effectively.
 
• These are fundamental skills for communication, education, and participation in society. It is not limited to reading or writing alone.
 
• Most countries and international organizations, including the UNESCO, define literacy as the ability to read and write simple statements or text in any language, even if the person is not fully fluent in that language.
 
• The literacy rate is typically calculated for individuals above a certain age, usually 15 years and older, to assess the educational attainment of a country or region.
 
• The standard definition of literacy may vary slightly depending on local contexts and educational systems, but the core concept remains the ability to **read and write**.

• The tertiary sector is often known as the **service industry.**
 
• It makes the most contribution to India's GDP, **more than 50%.**
 
• The tertiary sector is made up of the market services sector and the non-market services sector.
 
• Examples of Tertiary Sector

• **Real estate and Business services**

questions.question: In which state of India was the first train introduced in the year 1853?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maharashtra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The first passenger train in India ran on **16 April 1853**, from Bori Bunder in Mumbai to Thane.
 
• The train covered a distance of **34 kilometers** (21 miles).
 
• This historic train journey marked the beginning of the railway system in India, which was **introduced by the British** during their colonial rule.
 
• The train was operated by the **Great Indian Peninsula Railway (GIPR)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Great Indian Peninsula Railway (GIPR)**

 
 
• The GIPR was a predecessor of the Central Railway, which is one of the zones of Indian Railways.
 
• It was one of the first railway companies to be established in India.
 
• The GIPR played a crucial role in the development of the railway network in the western part of India.
 
• It was initially set up to connect the port city of Mumbai with the interior regions for the transportation of goods and passengers.
 
 
 
• **Indian Railways**
 
 
• Indian Railways is one of the largest railway networks in the world, owned and operated by the Government of India through the Ministry of Railways.
 
• It operates both long-distance and suburban rail systems on a multi-gauge network of broad, meter, and narrow gauges.
 
• Indian Railways is known for its extensive network that covers almost the entire country, providing connectivity to remote and rural areas.
 
• The railway network plays a vital role in the economic development of India, facilitating the movement of goods and passengers across the country.
 
 
 
• **Colonial Railways**
 
 
• The introduction of railways in India was a significant aspect of British colonial infrastructure development.
 
• The railways were primarily built to serve the economic and administrative interests of the British Empire.
 
• They facilitated the transport of raw materials from the interior to the ports and the movement of British troops.
 
• Despite the colonial motives, the railways eventually became a crucial part of India's transportation system and contributed to the country's social and economic integration.

questions.question: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) was established on:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mon Apr 01 1935 00:00:00 GMT+0530 (India Standard Time)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) was established on **1st April 1935**.
 
• RBI is the **central banking institution of India**, which controls the issuance and supply of the Indian rupee.
 
• It was initially set up in **Calcutta (now Kolkata)** but was permanently moved to **Mumbai in 1937**.
 
• The establishment of RBI was recommended by the **Hilton Young Commission in 1926**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Role and Functions of RBI**

 
 
• The RBI performs various developmental and promotional functions such as **controlling monetary policy**, **regulating and supervising financial systems**, and managing the country's foreign exchange.
 
• It acts as the **banker's bank** and **custodian of foreign exchange**.
 
• The RBI is responsible for **formulating and implementing India's monetary policy** to ensure price stability and adequate flow of credit to productive sectors.
 
• It also plays a critical role in **regulating and supervising the financial system** to ensure financial stability and public confidence in the system.
 
 
 
• **History of RBI**
 
 
• The RBI was initially set up as a private entity but was **nationalized in 1949**.
 
• It was established following the recommendations of the **Hilton Young Commission**.
 
• The original headquarters of RBI was in **Calcutta (Kolkata)** before moving to **Mumbai**.
 
• The RBI's central office is located in Mumbai, where the Governor sits and policies are formulated.
 
 
 
• **Structure of RBI**
 
 
• The RBI is managed by a central board of directors appointed by the Government of India.
 
• The board is comprised of a Governor, **four Deputy Governors**, and other directors appointed by the government.
 
• The Governor is the chief executive of the RBI and is responsible for its overall direction and control.
 
• The current Governor of RBI (as of October 2023) is **Shaktikanta Das**.

questions.question: In which state is the Kanha National Park located?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Madhya Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Kanha National Park is located in the state of Madhya Pradesh, India.
 
• It was established in 1955 and is one of the largest national parks in central India.
 
• Kanha National Park is known for its significant population of Bengal tigers, Indian leopards, sloth bears, barasingha, and Indian wild dogs.
 
• The park is spread over an area of approximately 940 square kilometers and is part of the larger Kanha Tiger Reserve.
 
• Kanha National Park inspired Rudyard Kipling's famous novel "The Jungle Book."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Flora and Fauna**

 
 
• Kanha is home to over 1000 species of flowering plants. The forest is a mixture of sal and other mixed forest trees.
 
• It is also known for its vast grasslands and meadows, known locally as "maidans."
 
• Besides tigers, Kanha supports a significant population of other wildlife like barasingha (swamp deer), gaur (Indian bison), and a variety of bird species.
 
 
 
• **Conservation Efforts**
 
 
• Kanha National Park has been a pioneer in wildlife conservation in India, notably for the barasingha conservation project which successfully increased their numbers.
 
• The park is part of Project Tiger, which was initiated in 1973 to ensure a viable population of tigers in their natural habitats.
 
 
 
• **Tourism**
 
 
• Kanha is a popular destination for wildlife enthusiasts and offers various safari options to explore its rich biodiversity.
 
• Tourists can enjoy jeep safaris, elephant safaris, and guided tours within the park.
 
• The park is divided into four zones: Kanha, Kisli, Mukki, and Sarhi, each offering unique wildlife viewing experiences.
 
 
 
• **Accessibility**
 
 
• Kanha National Park is well connected by road and is accessible from major cities like Jabalpur, Nagpur, and Raipur.
 
• The nearest airport is in Jabalpur, approximately 160 kilometers away, and the nearest railway station is in Gondia, around 145 kilometers from the park.

• **Beriberi**

 
 
• **Beriberi is a disorder** that can occur when a person has a** lack of thiamine or vitamin B-1.**
 
• A severe deficiency in this nutrient can lead to lasting damage to the nervous system and heart.
 
• There are two main forms of beriberi:** **
 
 
• **Wet beriberi, which mainly affects the cardiovascular system**
 
• **Dry beriberi, which primarily affects the nervous system**

• Clotting is a process that helps prevent excessive bleeding both inside and outside the body.

• It is also essential for the** normal function of blood vessels.**

questions.question: Who among the following Gurus of Sikh religion was the last Guru?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Guru Gobind Singh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Guru Gobind Singh was the **10th and last of the Sikh Gurus**.
 
• He was born on **22 December 1666** in Patna, Bihar, India.
 
• Guru Gobind Singh founded the **Khalsa in 1699**, which played a significant role in the religious and military history of the Sikhs.
 
• He introduced the **Five Ks (Kesh, Kangha, Kara, Kachera, Kirpan)**, which are the five articles of faith that Khalsa Sikhs must wear at all times.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Guru Angad**

 
 
• He was the **second Sikh Guru**, succeeding Guru Nanak.
 
• Guru Angad is credited with **standardizing the Gurmukhi script**, which became the script for the Punjabi language.
 
 
 
• **Guru Amar Das**
 
 
• He was the **third Sikh Guru**.
 
• Guru Amar Das is known for establishing **Manji and Piri systems of religious administration** in Sikhism.
 
• He also started the tradition of **Langar** (community kitchen) in Sikh temples.
 
 
 
• **Guru Hargobind**
 
 
• He was the **sixth Sikh Guru**.
 
• Guru Hargobind is notable for introducing the concept of **Miri and Piri** (temporal and spiritual authority).
 
• He wore two swords, representing both temporal and spiritual power.
 
 
 
• **Guru Gobind Singh**
 
 
• He was the **tenth and last Sikh Guru**.
 
• Guru Gobind Singh initiated the Khalsa and declared the **Guru Granth Sahib** as the eternal Guru of the Sikhs after him.

questions.question: At independence, which was the major employment-producing sector?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Agriculture**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• He also played a significant role in the founding of the London Indian Society and the East India Association, both of which aimed at raising awareness of Indian issues in Britain.

• The book argued that British policies were causing widespread poverty in India by draining wealth from the country.
 
• Naoroji introduced the concept of the "drain theory," which posited that the British were extracting wealth from India to benefit Britain, leading to the impoverishment of India.
 
• The book was influential in shaping Indian nationalist thought and provided a strong intellectual foundation for the Indian independence movement.

• Post-independence, the INC became the dominant political party in India, leading the country for several decades.

• Following the Indian Rebellion of 1857, the British Crown took direct control of India, leading to the establishment of the British Raj.
 
• British policies in India were often exploitative, focusing on extracting resources and wealth for the benefit of Britain.
 
• The economic, social, and political impact of British rule led to significant changes in Indian society and laid the groundwork for the independence movement.
